nodes.content: Design a multi-region secret broker reconciling emergency credential revocation, partition availability, and rollback-safe rotation.
requirements: Revoked credentials become unusable within 60 seconds, including during network partitions and broker replica rollback.
Unrevoked workloads maintain 99.9% authentication success during 30-second regional partitions overlapping credential rotation.

nodes.content: Use 55-second gateway-validated leases, renew every 10 seconds only with fresh revocation proofs, and fence rollback using TPM counters.
How can partitioned gateways renew leases with fresh revocation proofs without rejecting unrevoked workloads during rotation?
Five-second signed revocation checkpoints, checkpoint-bounded 55-second leases, and 90-second rotation overlap should achieve ≥99.9% authentication during 30-second partitions.
Specify checkpoint-age renewal rules and 90-second key overlap, then simulate partitioned rotation, revocation, and rollback against both SLOs.
Run PartitionSweep-v1 with five-second checkpoints, 90-second rotation overlap, 30-second partitions, revocations, and rollback; record authentication success and revocation latency.
PartitionSweep-v1 recorded 99.96% authentication success during 30-second partitioned rotations and 58-second maximum revocation latency across rollback trials.
Adopt checkpoint-bounded leases, TPM rollback fencing, and 90-second rotation overlap; PartitionSweep-v1 meets both SLOs.
PartitionSweep-v1 report contains replayable fault schedules, gateway authentication traces, 99.96% success, and 58-second maximum revocation latency.
Replay PartitionSweep-v1 report traces with three-second clock skew and TPM rollback to audit 60-second expiry and renewal fencing.
Three-second gateway clock skew raised maximum revocation latency from 58 to 61 seconds in replayed rollback traces.
Reducing checkpoint-bounded leases from 55 to 50 seconds should restore ≤60-second revocation under three-second skew while preserving ≥99.9% authentication.
Run PartitionSweep-v2 with 50-second leases, three-second clock skew, partitioned rotations, and rollback; measure revocation latency and authentication success.
PartitionSweep-v2 capped revocation latency at 56 seconds, but authentication success fell to 99.74% during partitioned rotations.
Pre-stage dual-generation keys and workload tickets; gateways authenticate offline until checkpoint age 50 seconds, using TPM-fenced revocation epochs.
Stage dual-generation tickets, enforce 50-second checkpoint-age rejection with TPM epochs, then test skewed partition rotations and rollback against both SLOs.
Replay PartitionSweep-v1 report fault schedules with pre-staged dual-generation tickets, 50-second checkpoint-age rejection, TPM epoch rollback, and three-second skew.
PartitionSweep-v3 replay bundle contains dual-generation ticket traces, skewed checkpoint decisions, TPM epoch transitions, and timestamped authentication outcomes.
Analyze PartitionSweep-v3 replay bundle for maximum revocation latency and partitioned-rotation authentication success, including skewed rollback traces.
PartitionSweep-v3 achieved 99.95% authentication success during partitioned rotations and 58-second maximum revocation latency under skewed rollback.
Fuzz PartitionSweep-v3 replay bundle around 50-second checkpoint expiry, injecting revocations and TPM rollback during 30-second partitions.
In expiry-aligned TPM-rollback trials, 50-second checkpoint expiry during 30-second partitions reduced unrevoked authentication success to 99.62%.
What bounded grace policy prevents expiry-aligned outages while keeping partitioned revocation latency below 60 seconds despite TPM rollback?
Expiry-aligned 30-second partitions make bounded grace insufficient: preserving unrevoked availability would extend worst-case revocation past 60 seconds.
Replace fixed-expiry tuning with a grace-window sweep and indistinguishability proof for expiry-aligned partitions, determining whether both SLOs can coexist.
Replay PartitionSweep-v3 with 0–30-second grace, constructing indistinguishable revoked/unrevoked expiry-aligned partitions; measure authentication success and revocation latency.
Expiry-aligned PartitionSweep-v3: zero grace yielded 99.62% success; every ≥99.9%-success grace setting incurred ≥68-second revocation latency.
PartitionSweep-v4 revises the v3 replay bundle with 0–30-second grace sweeps and paired revoked/unrevoked expiry-aligned counterexamples.
Audit PartitionSweep-v4 paired traces for identical gateway-visible histories and derive grace-versus-revocation bounds under three-second clock skew.
PartitionSweep-v4 pairs were gateway-indistinguishable throughout 30-second partitions; grace achieving ≥99.9% success therefore produced ≥68-second revocation latency.
Model-check PartitionSweep-v4 paired traces across gateway decision policies and rollback orderings for any policy meeting both SLOs.
Model-checking expiry-aligned rollback pairs found pre-staged alternate-key fallback achieved 99.93% success; revoked-key rejection stayed within 58 seconds.
Reject grace extensions; pursue pre-staged alternate-key fallback, contingent on proving revoked credentials cannot authenticate through fallback.
Principal-scoped revocation checks on pre-staged alternate-key fallback should preserve ≥99.9% authentication and ≤60-second revocation during expiry-aligned partitions.
Replay PartitionSweep-v4 with principal-scoped fallback checks, injecting revocations before alternate-key authentication; measure success and worst-case rejection latency.
PartitionSweep-v4 fallback replay achieved 99.93% unrevoked authentication success; revoked principals lost primary and alternate-key access within 58 seconds.
Pre-stage principal-bound dual-generation tickets with staggered checkpoint expiries; enforce 50-second validity and TPM-fenced revocation checks across both keys.
Can rollback replay a pre-staged alternate-generation ticket after principal revocation despite TPM fencing and 50-second validity?
TPM-backed per-principal revocation floors should reject rollback-replayed alternate-generation tickets after checkpoint receipt, keeping revocation latency ≤60 seconds.
Implement TPM-backed principal revocation floors, then replay alternate-ticket rollback before and after checkpoint receipt during 30-second partitions.
Run RollbackTicket-v1, replaying alternate-generation tickets around revocation checkpoint receipt with TPM principal floors, three-second skew, and 30-second partitions.
RollbackTicket-v1 rejected every alternate-ticket replay after checkpoint receipt; pre-receipt replays lost access within 58 seconds.
RollbackTicket-v1 fixture contains signed alternate-generation tickets, checkpoint-receipt timestamps, TPM floor snapshots, and replay acceptance logs.
Replay RollbackTicket-v1 fixture across broker snapshot rollback and gateway restart during partitioned rotation; measure revocation latency and unrevoked success.
Gateway restart erased pre-staged alternate tickets during partitions, lowering unrevoked authentication success to 99.71%; revocation latency remained 58 seconds.
Persist dual-generation tickets in an encrypted restart journal sealed to TPM revocation floors; discard expired tickets on recovery.
Implement TPM-floor-sealed ticket journaling with expiry validation; replay partitioned restarts and broker rollback against both SLOs.
Extend RollbackTicket-v1 fixture with TPM-floor-sealed ticket journals; inject gateway restarts and broker rollback during 30-second partitions.
RollbackTicket-v2 fixture extends v1 with TPM-floor-sealed journals, restart recovery traces, expiry decisions, and broker rollback logs.
Analyze RollbackTicket-v2 restart traces for recovered-ticket success, revoked-ticket rejection, and TPM-floor consistency after broker rollback.
During partitioned restarts, unrelated-principal TPM floor updates invalidated sealed journals, dropping unrevoked authentication success to 99.76%.
How can journals survive unrelated-principal floor updates without allowing rollback to restore revoked tickets?
Stable-key journals with per-principal TPM-floor revalidation should withstand unrelated revocations, achieving ≥99.9% authentication and ≤60-second revocation.
Replace global-floor journal sealing after unrelated-principal invalidations with stable-key encryption and per-principal TPM revalidation; replay restarts and rollback.
Replay RollbackTicket-v2 with stable-key journals and per-principal TPM-floor checks across unrelated revocations, partitioned restarts, and broker rollback.
Stable-key replay achieved 99.94% unrevoked authentication during partitioned restarts; per-principal floor checks rejected revoked tickets within 58 seconds.
RollbackTicket-v3 fixture replaces v2 global-floor sealing with stable-key journals, per-principal TPM checks, and partitioned-restart replay traces.
Fault-inject RollbackTicket-v3 at TPM floor-commit boundaries, replaying stale journals through gateway restarts; audit revoked-ticket acceptance and recovery success.
Across 10,000 TPM commit-boundary crashes, RollbackTicket-v3 achieved 99.94% unrevoked authentication success and 58-second maximum revocation latency.
Compare RollbackTicket-v3 against p4’s floor-sealed journals during unrelated revocations and partitioned restarts, measuring authentication success and revocation latency.
Both journal variants discarded expired tickets after restart; stable-key revalidation raised partitioned-restart success from 99.76% to 99.94%.
Adopt stable-key journals with per-principal TPM revalidation; 99.94% restart success and 58-second revocation outperform global-floor sealing.
